## How I work

**Read → implement in Colab → record what I learned → commit to GitHub.**

The website is the map. GitHub stores the notebooks and history. Colab is where the code runs.

## A simple daily study loop

I follow [Sebastian Raschka’s framework for getting the most from a technical book](https://sebastianraschka.com/blog/2025/reading-books.html):

1. **Read offline for 20 minutes** to understand the big picture.
2. **Read again with code** in Colab; type and run the important parts.
3. **Attempt one exercise** before checking the solution.
4. **Review what is still unclear** and write the useful explanation in [ML.ipynb](https://github.com/jooonkim/ml/blob/main/ML.ipynb).
5. **Use the idea** by changing one thing or applying it to a small experiment.

Every session ends with three lines in the notebook: **what I learned**, **what is still unclear**, and **what I will try next**.

```text
[ ] Read without coding
[ ] Run one small code section
[ ] Try one exercise or change
[ ] Write the takeaway and next step
[ ] Save to GitHub
```
